note: Public corrections log. material=true means it affected a number a reader could have acted on. Entries are permanent.

entries.what: Wizards Black Star Promo birds were dated 1999. They are 2000.
entries.claim: The catalogue, the editor year field, and the 2026-08-27 post '1999 and 2026 — 27 years apart' all used pokemontcg.io's SET start (1999/07/01) for every Wizards promo. @dank_porygon corrected it. PSA slabs print 2000. Bulbapedia: Power of One theatrical giveaway, 21 July 2000, second week.
entries.detail: pokemontcg.io stores one releaseDate per set. Wizards Black Star Promos ran July 1999–March 2003, so all 53 cards inherited 1999. Same shape on Nintendo/DP/BW/SM/SWSH/SVP Black Star Promos. Main-set dates (Ruby & Sapphire 2003, Neo Revelation 2001) were already card-accurate because those sets dropped on one day.
entries.whatChanged: data/release-date-overrides.json holds per-card English dates for all 53 Wizards promos from Bulbapedia. ingest-catalogue.mjs reapplies them after every API pull. build-editor.mjs writes the override year into the index. Year-span captions skip Black Star promo sets that have no override. Editor hostile test: basep-21/22/23 year is 2000.
entries.caughtBy: Tyler, from the reply. The live page and the catalogue agreed with each other and with the API, and they were all wrong.
entries.guardAdded: Per-card overlay plus yearOk(): do not print 'N years apart' from a Black Star promo set-start date.

entries.what: Our marketplace gap was not comparing like with like. The eBay figure included shipping; TCGplayer market prices do not. On cheap items — packs especially — this reversed the answer: we showed some packs asking far more on eBay when, once shipping was counted on both sides, they were actually cheaper there.
entries.fix: Both sides now include shipping and neither includes tax, which is stated wherever a price appears. Journey Together booster packs moved from +54.9% to -12.7%; Destined Rivals from +7.5% to -30%. Sealed boxes barely changed, because both marketplaces ship those free.
entries.guard: The comparison basis is recorded on every row, and the shipping estimate is labelled as an estimate with a stated condition for re-checking it.

entries.what: Our Pokemon GO Elite Trainer Box figure read high. Multi-quantity listings ("lot of 2", "2x", sealed cases) were passing our filters and lifting medians on any product with an active lot market.
entries.fix: The product is held out of published reads until it re-verifies. The filter now rejects multi-item listings across all 207 products.
entries.guard: A multi-item pattern guard runs at fetch time, and a durable quarantine file keeps a held product held even through a full data rebuild.

entries.what: Share cards were minted in a format social platforms reject, and long text inside them was being dropped when converted.
entries.fix: Cards now render as PNG with the text drawn natively.
entries.guard: Every card rasterizes as part of the daily run, so the format that ships is the format that was checked.

entries.what: Our sealed index baseline included the day we changed pricing methods, so part of the first move measured our own cleanup rather than the market.
entries.fix: The baseline was moved to the first full day under the current method and the history rebuilt from source snapshots.
entries.guard: New sets also sit out their first 90 days, so launch-window noise never enters the index.

entries.what: The Spread has been retired from the front page
entries.detail: We compared our eBay prices against TCGplayer prices for the same product and used that gap to help choose what we put in front of you. The two figures are not measured the same way: ours includes delivery, theirs is an item price with shipping excluded, and no shipping-inclusive TCGplayer figure is available to us at any price. The gap therefore always read wider than the real difference, and worst on cheap products where postage is most of the cost. It no longer chooses the Daily Three and no longer raises signals. It stays on product pages as a labelled stat, because two marketplaces disagreeing is still worth seeing.
entries.whatChanged: Removed from the Daily Three selection and from the signal list. Kept as a labelled stat on product pages with a permanent note that the TCGplayer figure excludes shipping. Methodology page rewritten to explain the demotion.

entries.what: The 122x posting-hour finding is withdrawn. It compared one post against itself at two different ages.
entries.claim: data/post-outcomes.json stated: 'on 2026-08-22 the identical pairing post did 154 views at a bad hour and 18,800 at 9:18pm — 122x, same cards, same caption, same format.' That number was repeated in commit 9551bde as a lesson learned about timing confounding format.
entries.detail: There were never two posts. There was one post, entered twice. Both entries carried the same postedAt of 21:18, and the second was labelled 'REPOST at 9:18pm' — but 9:18pm IS 21:18, so the entry describing the repost was describing the original. The 154 views were read twelve minutes after posting. The 18,800 were read fifteen hours and twenty minutes after posting. A post is not 122 times better at a different hour; it is 122 times bigger fifteen hours later, which is what every post does. The first correction claimed to have found a confound and introduced a worse one: it fixed a comparison across hours by writing a law about hours, when the actual defect was a comparison across ages.
entries.whatChanged: The two entries are merged into one post with a three-reading time series at 0.2h, 15.33h and 59.8h. The note claiming 122x is deleted. The law is replaced with: 'Readings are only comparable at equal age. Compare 48h to 48h. Any comparison across different measurement ages is measuring age.' Every reading now records its real atHours so the age is impossible to overlook.
entries.caughtBy: TYLER, FROM A SCREENSHOT. He opened the live post, saw one status where the log claimed two, and said so. The machines did not catch it — they had the same postedAt written twice in a file they both read, computed a 122x ratio from it, wrote a law on top of it, committed that law as a lesson about intellectual honesty in small samples, and then cited it in later sessions as settled. Three passes over the same six-line file, none of which compared two timestamps that were identical.
entries.alsoFound: The same defect runs through the whole file, and the Arita pair was only the visible instance. The remaining readings were taken at 25.02h (Charmander, 791 views), -0.06h (Slakoth, 124 views) and 0.03h (Sunflora, 93 views) — a reading taken 1.7 minutes after posting was ranked against one taken a day later. Every shape comparison this log has ever produced was across unequal ages.

entries.what: Every hand-typed timestamp in post-outcomes.json was a Pacific wall clock with a Z on the end.
entries.claim: postedAt values such as '2026-08-22T21:18:00Z' were treated as UTC by everything that read them, including the posting-hour analysis whose entire subject is what time of day a post goes out.
entries.detail: 21:18 in Vancouver is 04:18 UTC the following day, so the recorded instants were seven hours out and on the wrong calendar date for anything posted after 5pm local. The file mixed two conventions with no marker: values written by new Date().toISOString() were genuine UTC, values typed by a human were local, and the only tell was whether the string carried milliseconds. Proven rather than assumed, using git commit times, which are real UTC: the entry recording a reading at '2026-08-22T21:30:00Z' was committed at 04:30:16Z, sixteen seconds later once 21:30 is read as Pacific; the entry recording '2026-08-23T19:37:31.524Z' was committed at 19:39:04Z, ninety-three seconds later with no conversion. One entry resisted both readings and was settled a third way: pmt8ossvc's id encodes Date.now() in base36 and decodes to 2026-08-25T13:14:41.832Z, so reading its 11:12:00Z as local would place the post five hours after the entry that logged it and two hours in the future.
entries.whatChanged: All five posts converted to true UTC with an explicit tz, plus hourLocal and postedAtLocal so the wall clock survives — '9pm' is the thing being tested and nobody thinks in 04:18Z. scripts/lib/timestamp.mjs now owns every conversion, uses the zone database rather than a hardcoded -7 so it does not break in November, and refuses to record a timestamp without an explicit tz. It also rejects a post dated in the future and a reading dated before its own post, which are the two shapes this bug takes that are decidable from the data alone.
entries.caughtBy: Tyler: 'our timestamps are local time wearing a Z.' The guard exists because the string itself cannot tell you which convention it came from — that information was never written down, which is the whole defect. A guard that tried to infer it would be guessing.

entries.what: A settled-value error propagated into stated laws. The Arita pairing was quoted at 18,800 views in seventeen places; it settled at 127,200.
entries.claim: 18,800 views was written into research/house-theses.md five times, the Notice register definition in the line engine, the layout label a user reads when choosing 'the pairing', a theme description in data/themes.json, a running experiment arm, two agent-competence statements, a knowledge.json fact, and the editor page built from all of them. It was presented throughout as what the post DID.
entries.detail: 18,800 was the reading at 15h20m, taken while the post was still climbing. The settled 48h reading is 127,200 views, 2,500 likes, 34 replies, 86 reposts, 170 bookmarks - the quoted figure understated the post by 6.8x. THE NUMBER DID NOT SIT STILL: research/house-theses.md built a law on top of it, stating that reach relative to account size is the metric and that Tyler was 'already in this company' beside Crambo's 2.1x. That claim was never computed. @LongedEth has 21,554 followers (X API, 2026-08-25), so 18,800 was 0.87x his follower count - BELOW Crambo, the opposite of what the passage asserted from it. The settled 127,200 is 5.90x, or 2.8x Crambo's ratio. A passage whose entire subject was a ratio contained no ratio, and the wrong number was load-bearing for a law that happened to be right for reasons nobody had checked.
entries.whatChanged: All seventeen occurrences corrected or explicitly marked as withdrawn. The reach law now shows its arithmetic. The Notice register keeps its characterisation - a register is defined by the SENTENCE, not the view count, so the correction left it untouched and strengthened its evidence, since 127,200 is settled where 18,800 was mid-climb; it remains n=1. scripts/build-lines.mjs regenerates scripts/line-engine.js, which build-editor.mjs embeds into research/assets/build.html, so the generator was edited and both artifacts rebuilt rather than hand-patched. A running experiment in data/experiments.json had arm a at 18,800 (15.33h) against arm b at 791 (25.02h) and is now marked unreadable: both arms unsettled at different ages, which is the same error one level down.
entries.caughtBy: Tyler, from the settled screenshot. The machines had every input needed - post-outcomes.json carried all three readings with their real atHours - and no check compared a number written in prose against the number in the log.
entries.guardAdded: verify-work.mjs error class 'stale metric': once a post has a settled 48h reading, every earlier reading of the same post is a dead number, and quoting one anywhere outside an explicit withdrawal is a defect. It found four propagation sites that the manual audit had missed - data/agent-competence.json (x2), data/experiments.json and data/knowledge.json. Negative-proven: a temporary file quoting 18,800 was flagged, and removing it cleared the finding.
entries.alsoFound: Only ONE of the five logged posts has a settled 48h reading at all. The others were read at 25.02h, 0.03h and -0.06h - the last of those being a reading timestamped BEFORE its own post. The three-register evidence block ranked a 1.7-minute-old reading against a two-and-a-half-day-old one; the numbers are now printed with their ages so the comparison cannot be made silently again.
entries.alsoFound2: scripts/build-lines.mjs is in no workflow. It is the GENERATOR for scripts/line-engine.js, which ships inside the editor, so the shipped copy only updates when someone runs the generator by hand and can silently drift from its source. The repo's own steward-report already lists build-lines.mjs among 14 unreferenced scripts; that report was right, and the consequence was not understood.

entries.what: Three posts were written off on readings taken minutes after they went out. The claim built on them was not understated - it was backwards.
entries.claim: house-theses.md, catchem-knowledge-base.md, agent-competence.json and themes.json all stated that cropped card art with a two-word hook beat a carefully constructed artist pairing five to one, same account, same week: 791 views against 154. house-theses also called the crop 'the best-performing thing we have made' and said the evidence 'points away from the direction we were building'.
entries.detail: Every figure was a reading age. The 154 was taken twelve minutes after posting, the 124 at four minutes, the 93 at under two. Settled at 48h and read from the API: Arita pairing 127,200, Slakoth 941, Sunflora 926, Charmander 867. THE PAIRING DID NOT LOSE BY FIVE TIMES, IT WON BY A HUNDRED AND FORTY-SEVEN. Slakoth and Sunflora were treated as failures for three days on numbers that measured how fast a page loaded; Slakoth now outperforms the crop that was being held up as the success. The three crops land within 74 views of each other, which is to say they are indistinguishable, and no conclusion about mood hooks, share prompts or 2am posting survives from them.
entries.whatChanged: The reach claim is withdrawn and reversed in all four files. Art mode keeps its place on the reasons that were never about reach - Tyler asked for it, and the artwork is the content. Every remaining citation of an unsettled view count now names the age it was read at; twelve were found and fixed across house-theses.md, agent-competence.json, community.json, themes.json, build-creators-page.mjs, card-composite.mjs, log-outcome.mjs and outcome-report.mjs. All readings under 1h now carry belowFloor:true and are excluded from analysis by outcome-report.
entries.caughtBy: The API. The backfill made the settled numbers visible for the first time, and they contradicted the stated law. No human and no guard caught this in the three days it stood.
entries.guardAdded: verify-work class 'unsettled view count': a view count from a reading that has not settled may only appear beside the age it was read at, or beside a withdrawal. It is deliberately NARROWER than the stale-metric class rather than larger - stale-metric ignores values under 1,000 to avoid noise from a card catalogue, and every figure in this incident was under 1,000, which is exactly how it slipped through. This one fires only on lines talking about views. Negative-proven both ways.
entries.alsoFound: Two defects in the guard layer itself. verify-work's shared helpers were block-scoped, so the next guard to use them threw ReferenceError - and the file still wrote its report and still exited, so a guard that could not run at all looked exactly like a guard that found nothing. And the context window looked five lines back but only three forward, which flags a correctly-withdrawn passage, because a withdrawal always FOLLOWS the claim it withdraws.

entries.what: The age-comparability guard was an over-correction and was discarding valid data. A guard that throws away good readings is a failure too, just a quieter one.
entries.claim: assertComparable refused any two readings more than 10% apart in age. The outcome report therefore declared four posts SETTLED and then answered its central question using only two of them, excluding Charmander at 85.0h and Sunflora at 48.2h for having ages incomparable to the 59h pair.
entries.detail: Both cannot be true. SETTLED_AT is 48h, and 48h was chosen precisely because views have largely flattened by then - so the entire point of the threshold is that readings past it are comparable. The rule was written after comparing a TWELVE MINUTE reading against a TWENTY-TWO HOUR one, two orders of magnitude apart on a curve still climbing steeply. That lesson was right and the rule generalised it too far: 48h against 85h is not that comparison. NOBODY FILES A BUG ABOUT AN ANSWER THEY NEVER SAW, which is what makes this failure mode quieter than the one it was guarding against.
entries.whatChanged: Two readings both at or past 48h are now comparable, and the age is printed beside every figure so a reader can judge the spread instead of trusting that someone checked. SETTLED_HOURS moved into lib/timestamp.mjs, which two files were each keeping their own copy of. What did NOT change: a settled reading may still never be compared against an unsettled one. That was the actual defect and it is still refused.
entries.effect: The reach-versus-density answer is unchanged - reach and density still diverge - but it now rests on FOUR settled posts instead of two, and the density leader moves from Slakoth at 10.63 per thousand to Charmander at 16.15. The shape comparison went from refusing outright to reporting the art crop family at n=3, mean 911 views and mean 12.16 replies per thousand. Both were available the whole time and were being withheld.
entries.caughtBy: Tyler, reading the report and noticing it called four posts settled and then used two.
